target_customer: Underrepresented high school students (free), funded by foundations, corporate sponsors and grants
problem: Girls, ethnic minorities and other underrepresented high schoolers lack access to coding education and to the tech talent pipeline.
business_model: 501(c)(3) nonprofit funded by grants and donations; free workshops

founders.name: Ryan Seashore
founders.background_notes: Per YC page and YC blog. ProPublica Form 990 data as summarized in a search result lists him as CEO until March 2017, with Neal Sales-Griffin of Starter League taking over as CEO.

technical_complexity.rationale: A workshop program, not a software product; the difficulty was curriculum, volunteers and logistics.

defensibility.rationale: Workshops and curriculum were copyable; its edge was a network of volunteers and funders.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquirer; as a nonprofit it changed leadership in 2016 to 2017 and the YC page still lists it as active.

market_need_then: YC described the mission as teaching programming basics to high schoolers, especially girls and minorities; launched in Washington DC in 2011 and expanded to New York and San Francisco in 2013 per the YC blog.

branding.domain_note: Uses codenow.org. Note an unrelated software company also uses the name CodeNOW at a different domain.
branding.community_and_virality: White House coverage in 2011 and Awesome Foundation grant listed in search results; not read in depth.

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand material found; the name is generic and shares itself with another company.

outcome_analysis: CodeNow was part of YC's first batch of nonprofits and ran workshops for underrepresented high schoolers, expanding with a $100,000 Knight Foundation grant in 2014. Public information after the 2016 to 2017 CEO change is thin, so the long run outcome is unclear and this record cannot judge success or failure.
notes: Nonprofit; not a venture company. YC nonprofit grant reported by Crunchbase News as $100,000 no-equity, and an aggregator lists $120K dated 2014-03-25; both unverified for CodeNow specifically so not recorded. Competitor list empty: no source dated near 2014 names rivals. The current codenow.org site as fetched describes a different software company (CodeNOW), so the website no longer reflects the nonprofit; treat as a dead or repurposed domain. Founder education and prior employers not found.
